label: sec:complex-volume-ladder-intro
html:
The \beta-decay Q-value is the imaginary part of the complex volume \mathfrak{V}: \mathfrak{Q}_\beta = \mathrm{Im}\,\mathfrak{V}. It forms the bar-odd (\sinh) partner to the bar-even (\cosh) binding part \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}} = \mathrm{Re}\,\mathfrak{V}. This subsection develops its precision ladder—the convergent series \mathfrak{Q}_\beta = \mathfrak{Q}_{\mathrm{base}}\cdot\prod_k(1 + c_k u^k) with u = b\,\hbar_q^2—as the \mathrm{Im} leg of a complex-volume expansion whose \mathrm{Re} leg is the binding ladder.

The blocks present the categorical precision ladder, the c_3 = -2 Hopf three-fold Markov near-match, the c_k extraction from algebraic rules, the typed B_3 sub-braid extraction, and the geometric realization of the depth-3 period. The c_k are Taylor coefficients of the fibre-level complex \mathfrak{V}(q). The c_2 = -1 coefficient is Taylor-exact, while c_k for k \geq 3 are structural near-matches arising from a single complex-analytic coefficient evaluated at real q_0 along its two parities.
